newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen retreating in consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen retreating in consolidation.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to retreat in consolidation on Wednesday with uncertain investors clinging to the sidelines, brokers said.
"Consolidation is likely to continue for the time being to pave the way for further gains in the future," said Baek Jung-hyun of Samsung Securities.
The composite stock index closed Tuesday up 0.65 points at 753.70.
Margin loans at brokerage houses have recently moved ahead of customer deposits, which is likely to depress the market.
Brokers said margin loans had steadily risen to 3.32 trillion won as of Monday, while customer deposits, which had been shrinking for the past week, tallied at 3.31 trillion.
Blue chip counters are expected to be hit by profit-takers after a short rise on Tuesday, they said.

Brokers said a lack of foreign buying would keep the trading volume at thin levels. They said it is expected to worsen prior to the handover of Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30 as a lot of foreign orders arrive in South Korea via Hong Kong.
However, Chohung Bank will remain in the spotlight on Tuesday's news that 4.39 percent of the bank's outstanding common shares would become newly available for foreign investment from June 26.
"The market is expected to shed five to six points on an overall bearish mood," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
